title: LSTARENGY — Evidence-Led Sports Projection Research
description: Evidence-led research into LineStar's DFS projection product (linestarapp.com): a dated review of the vendor's own public product descriptions, an independent data-and-implementation plan, and a runnable projection prototype over synthetic data. The repository states in terms what it is not — not a recovered private algorithm, not a subscription bypass, not a production sports-data service, not a legal clearance and not a demonstrated match to LineStar's data quality — and its research snapshot is dated 2026-09-22 UTC with the note that build dates do not reset source observation dates. Every count here was read from the committed evidence register at 66d9c9b and re-confirmed by running the repository's own validator: 36 capability records (public claim, evidence references, sport and screen scope, access status, independent implementation status, required inputs, limitations), 30 source records distinguishing vendor, league, government, provider, platform and community-maintainer, each with an observation date, short excerpt, location, link and excerpt hash; 62 line-referenced legacy claim groups correcting the previous state of this repository against the immutable base commit 0ac0b07a; a 13-label coverage plan, nine input categories, 14 review flags, 10 findings and six prioritized next-work packages. `npm run check` was executed in this audit and passed all three of its gates: `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` reported 72 tests, 72 pass, 0 fail on Node v22.22.3; `scripts/validate.mjs` printed 'Traceability valid: 36 capabilities, 30 sources, 62 legacy review groups. This is not automated proof of source truth.'; and `scripts/build.mjs --check` printed 'Verified 22 deterministic site assets. Both main:/ and main:/docs entrypoints are supported.' A further 13 Playwright browser and accessibility specs exist in tests/browser/ and were not executed, because no browser binary is available in this audit environment. The published site is a 217,302-byte root index.html built from web/template.html with search, category and evidence filtering, deep citations, JSON and CSV downloads and no-JavaScript research content; the prototype is a deterministic lab doing recency-weighted mean forecasts, point-in-time filtering, historical quantiles, an exact small-pool lineup solver, locks and exclusions, optional QB stack, greedy multi-lineup diversity and exposure constraints, late-swap slot preservation, stale-data blocking and safe CSV export, evaluated walk-forward on fixtures with EV arithmetic from assumed rather than estimated probabilities. All lab athlete labels, scores, salaries, odds and event dates are test fixtures. The build, validator, unit tests and demo have no runtime package dependencies and need no network or credentials. The repository is 60 tracked files.

This entry was published as documentation-only and is now an application — the fourth stub-to-app reversal in this pass and the sixth this directory has recorded (IRR-42, IRR-64, IRR-72, IRR-84, IRR-90). At 0ac0b07 the repository was four files (README.md, docs/index.html, docs/styles.css, docs/.nojekyll) with no engine, no dataset and no tests; three commits and 60 files later (+18,628/-7,768) it has src/ (7 modules), tests/ (5 node test files plus a browser spec), scripts/ (5), web/ (5), research/ (5), two GitHub Actions workflows and a package.json. The previous description's central claim — that nothing in the repository reproduces or replays anything — was true when written and is false now.

The repository corrects this directory's own earlier prose, and the correction is published rather than quietly absorbed. This entry previously stated 'the published paywall pricing of 39.99 USD per month or 239.99 USD per year' as a single fact; the repository's corrections section now records that the web pricing page displays $239.99/year while the US DraftKings app listing displays $269.99/year, that these are dated offers and not verified checkout totals or a universal price, and that 'Perfect Lineups is not established as paid-only' because the vendor guide advertises a free historical view. It also withdraws two claims the earlier state of the repository made: that standard algorithms are generally non-infringing (removed) and that 'self-healing' evidences a reproducible nightly retraining algorithm (it does not).

Sourcing is stated as LineStar's own website, its official GitBook documentation, the Apple App Store and Google Play listings and Google Patents, with free-data alternatives cited from their official repositories; the README's rule is that a claim without an openable source is marked as a local observation. The four patent numbers the earlier entry listed (9,751,010; 9,744,450; 10,478,721; 11,660,533) are now explicitly qualified: patent ownership, scope and enforceability were not independently established, and the official USPTO review route is cited instead of an inference.

Legal and licensing barriers are recorded as real project gates rather than caveats: the published terms restrict automated access, reverse engineering, use of outputs for AI/ML and competitive use; no permission to ingest or redistribute LineStar outputs was obtained; and the project states it is not affiliated with or endorsed by LineStar, BetFully Inc., DraftKings, FanDuel or Yahoo.
